dedupe_keys.name: canada energy regulator pipeline incident data and interactive pipeline map 2008 to present

description: This data set lists incidents on federally regulated pipelines and processing plants in Canada reported to the Canada Energy Regulator (formerly the National Energy Board) under the Onshore Pipeline Regulations and Processing Plant Regulations, including cause information. It runs from 2008 to the present, is updated quarterly, and was last updated on the Open Government Portal on 2 September 2026. Fields include year, incident number, significance, occurrence, discovery and report dates, interruption duration, system type (transmission, gathering, distribution or processing), activity at the time, discovery method, status, company, equipment involved, rupture flag, incident type (fatality, serious injury, explosion, fire, release, operation beyond design limits, environmental effects), and released substance. The CER interactive pipeline map shows these incidents with pipeline locations covering about 90 percent of operating federally regulated pipelines as of March 2017. Coverage is Canada's interprovincial and international pipelines. The data are CSV files in English and French with a data dictionary, downloadable at no cost under the Open Government Licence - Canada. Caveats: provincially regulated lines are excluded, and the data dictionary still refers to the National Energy Board. Simulation uses are incident rates by cause and system type for pipeline risk and resilience models. Related records: data-egig-european-gas-pipeline-incident-database covers European gas transmission incidents.
